name: LA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with an R+18 partisan lean
Incumbent Clay Higgins has a massive fundraising advantage ($823K raised vs. under $25K for the top Democrat)
Prediction markets price Higgins at roughly 95% to win
No general-election polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: Higgins holds a deeply Republican seat, outspends the Democratic field by more than thirty to one, and markets give him about a 95% chance of reelection. With no polls or ratings suggesting vulnerability, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending against Higgins or a scandal-driven headline could narrow the race, though the district lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Louisiana's third district is a solidly Republican seat, and incumbent Clay Higgins is seeking another term with the advantages that come with it. He has raised over $820,000 and holds nearly $600,000 in cash, while the leading Democratic challenger, John Day, has raised about $23,000 with minimal cash on hand. No outside groups are spending in the race on either side.

There is no public general-election polling and no expert ratings for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and resources. Prediction markets give Higgins roughly a 95% chance of winning. The Democratic field is divided among several little-funded candidates, and nothing in the available evidence suggests the seat is in play.
